summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 6/38)

data.turoyo: Ḥəlle l Abu Zed, samiqi ʕayne w qrəṭle ʕaršone w lwəšle u zərh.
data.translation: Als Abu Sêd dies sah, röteten sich seine Augen vor Grimm; er knirschte mit den Zähnen und zog seinen Panzer an.

rationale: Thin Preterit; expanded tooth form ʕaršone and explicit anger context.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 27/19)

data.turoyo: Nxəšle a greʕe b ʕayne lu malko dam maymun, mqawmi aʕle ʕal u Bani Sabʕa. Mədle li xanǧar, qrəṭle ʕarše lu Bani Sabʕa, qṭile traḥṣar bu diwan.
data.translation: da winkte der König der Halbmenschen seinen Dienern mit den Augen, und sie umringten den Löwenkönig. Dieser aber griff zum Dolche, knirschte mit den Zähnen und tödtete zwölf von den Dienern im Empfangszimmer;

rationale: Thin Preterit; postverbal l-marked agent Bani Sabʕa and tooth object, with action sequence.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 28/30)

data.turoyo: Raxu aʕla abre d Rusṭam, u ǧənnawi kḥoyər, lo qodər qoyəm, qorəṭ ʕarše.
data.translation: Der Sohn Rustem's umarmte sie, der Dschennâwi musste es ansehen und konnte nicht aufstehen: er knirschte mit den Zähnen.

rationale: Thin Infectum; unprefixed qorəṭ with teeth, unlike existing stones example.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (56/117)

data.turoyo: Knofəl bayn aḥ ḥeṭe, koxəl w hiye kal ʕal ḥaṣe du ḥmoro koqorəṭ i qaḏ̣amaṯe.
data.translation: Er marschiert in den Weizen hinein und frißt, und der Löwentöter sitzt auf dem Rücken des Esels und knappert all die Kichererbsen auf.

rationale: Thin Infectum; literal food crunching as opposed to tooth-grinding and stone hyperbole.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (58/204)

data.turoyo: Ḥzeli, kala b dukṯo ʕatəmto. Kətla garmo xalyo, kale gmaḥwər b fema, kərkər diḏa koqərṭo ebe.
data.translation: Ich fand sie an einem finsteren Orte hausend. Sie hat einen leeren Knochen, der weiß an ihrem Munde schimmert. Sie beißt mit Zähnegeknirsch in ihn hinein.

rationale: b- bone target and manner noun kərkər motivate gloss clarification; preserve the full context.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (75/299)

data.turoyo: W annaqla qayimo, koqərṭo ak kefe, kosaymalle ʕuro b ʕarša.
data.translation: Da zerknirschte sie Steine mit den Zähnen und machte sie zu Spreu.

rationale: Fifth Infectum; feminine koqərṭo and stones reduced to chaff, an unusual emphatic context.

summary: New idiom: u qaṭuno b ḥəlme koqoraṭ ʕəbugre ‘die Katze zerbeißt Mäuse im Traum’ (Sprichwort für bloße Wunschvorstellungen)

data.headword: u qaṭuno b ḥəlme koqoraṭ ʕəbugre ‘die Katze zerbeißt Mäuse im Traum’ (Sprichwort für bloße Wunschvorstellungen)
data.turoyo: <...> Yaʕni u qaṭuno b ḥəlme koqoraṭ ʕəbugre. U qaṭuno mə d kodomax, koḥoze ḥəlme, koqoraṭ ʕəbugre. <...>
data.translation: <...> That is, the cat in its dream crunches mice. When the cat sleeps, it sees dreams, it crunches mice. <...>

rationale: Proverb is used for wishful thinking, as the following claim about obtaining Mesopotamia only in dreams makes explicit. Lookup koqoraṭ returned 0; qaṭuno b returned only an unrelated drowning example. Listed once as a phrase; no new verb sense or sixth routine Infectum example. English is the supplied project machine translation.

summary: Preterit shows L-marked agent inflection, with a postverbal l-marked nominal agent in PrS27/19; Infectum has zero-marked tooth/food/stone objects or b- target.
112/176 Infectum-wa is a hypothetical consequence of having an impossible quantity of chickpeas in the moment of tooth-chattering. It does not independently establish habitual past use.
The tooth construction is already represented by gloss knirschen and inherited examples. No new light-verb idiom is needed; do not confuse food crunching with another homonym solely from the object.
I Infectum 1 already has five examples after round 1; reader thin-cell rationale is stale. The proverb adds a new phrase, not another routine box example.

Repeated koqoraṭ belongs to one supplied verse and one proverb context. Preserve both occurrence decisions, but quote the proverb once. Homonym qrṭ 2 breakfast provides no better analysis for a cat crunching mice.
58/204: is kərkər diḏa a fronted manner/cognate phrase or a separate nominal predicate? b-e clearly supplies the bone target but the phrase's syntax needs confirmation.
Check old prs14/32 and prs88/27 against the assigned PrS6/24 and34/104 before changing citations; the short tooth formula alone is not a concordance.
Confirm the morphophonology of koqoraṭṭe75/112; the clearer feminine koqərṭo75/299 is selected, with no normalized replacement.
Is the printed cat/mice proverb a conventional fixed expression beyond this speaker, and does its usual form retain the repeated explanatory sentence? The supplied rhetorical use is clear.
Correct the mixed-script spelling of knirschte
rationale: The German word contains Cyrillic с (U+0441) instead of Latin c.

summary: Objects range from teeth in the grinding construction to chickpeas and hyperbolically crushed stones; b- marks the bone gnawed at. Anger, pain and fear motivate events without separate emotion senses.

An animal crunching mice in a dream is a participant extension of the existing biting meaning. The surrounding discourse makes the whole proverb figurative; the verb itself does not gain a political or dream-specific sense.
